headline: Monitor Road Access and Seasonal Camping Reservations
reservation: A National Park entry permit is required for all visitors. Due to high demand and environmental management, campsite reservations open months in advance and are essential for overnight stays; backcountry permits must be secured through the official Parks Canada portal. Always check for current wildfire-related closures or road restrictions that may affect the Icefields Parkway.

days.title: Canyons and Alpine Lakes

stops.name: Maligne Canyon
stops.detail: Walk the bridge system over the deepest canyon in the Canadian Rockies to see dramatic waterfalls and karst formations.

stops.name: Maligne Lake
stops.detail: Visit the largest glacially fed lake in the Rockies, famous for the Spirit Island vista.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours for the return Maligne Lake Road drive; conditions vary
days.note: Maligne Lake Road is a prime area for wildlife viewing; maintain a slow speed and do not feed animals.

days.title: Glacial Ice and High Passes

stops.name: Athabasca Falls
stops.detail: Observe the power of the Athabasca River as it thunders through a narrow quartzite gorge.

stops.name: Columbia Icefield
stops.detail: View the Athabasca Glacier from the Toe of the Glacier trail or the Discovery Centre.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 3 hours for the Icefields Parkway southward; conditions vary
days.note: Weather at the Icefield is significantly colder than the townsite; allow extra time for sudden snow or wind.

days.title: Peaks and Natural Springs

stops.name: Mount Edith Cavell
stops.detail: View the hanging Angel Glacier and the dramatic north face of the mountain from the Path of the Glacier trail.

stops.name: Miette Hot Springs
stops.detail: Soak in the hottest mineral springs in the Rockies located in the remote Fiddle Valley.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 2.5 hours total driving between these disparate sites; conditions vary
days.note: The road to Mount Edith Cavell has vehicle length restrictions and is seasonally closed until late June.

intel.title: Maligne Canyon Congestion
intel.text: The first and second bridge parking lots fill early; utilize the lower fifth bridge lot for a quieter approach to the canyon. At Mount Edith Cavell, parking is strictly limited to small vehicles.

intel.title: Icefields Parkway Dead Zones
intel.text: There is virtually no cellular service along Highway 93 between Jasper and Lake Louise. Download all maps and reservation confirmations for offline use.

intel.title: Strategic Refueling
intel.text: Fuel is available in the Jasper townsite and at the Saskatchewan River Crossing. Prices at the Crossing are typically higher due to its remote location.

intel.title: Cavell Road Openings
intel.text: The road to Mount Edith Cavell usually opens in mid-to-late June depending on snowpack. Check the Parks Canada 'Roads to Trails' report for exact seasonal status.

intel.title: Wildlife Corridors
intel.text: Seasonal speed limits and temporary area closures are frequently enforced to protect caribou and bear populations. Obey all posted signage near the Sunwapta Pass.

plan.arrival: Collect your rental at Edmonton (YEG) and complete major grocery shopping in Hinton or Edmonton before entering the park gates.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for the Icefields Parkway, but an RV offers convenience for the long distances between Jasper and Banff sites.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset at Pyramid Lake offers reflections of Pyramid Mountain, though the peaks may lose light earlier than expected in autumn.
